patterns.name: Hardcoded secret or credential in Python source
patterns.description: A string literal that looks like a credential (JWT secret, API key, password, database URL) is assigned directly in source rather than loaded from environment variables or a secret manager. This exposes credentials in version control.
patterns.message: Variable '{target}' in {file} contains what appears to be a hardcoded credential. Load secrets from os.environ or a secret manager instead.

patterns.name: Hardcoded fallback when environment variable is missing in Python
patterns.description: os.environ.get() or os.getenv() is called with a hardcoded default fallback, embedding a credential in source code for cases where the environment variable is absent. This pattern is extremely common in Python and frequently reaches production.
patterns.message: '{target}' in {file} uses a hardcoded fallback value when the environment variable is absent. Remove the default — raise a RuntimeError at startup if the required secret is not configured.
